overview.description: Design and assemble DNA at genome scale: minimal genomes (JCVI-syn3.0), the synthetic yeast Sc2.0, and whole-genome recoding to free up codons. Everything is hierarchical - oligos to genes to cassettes to chromosomes - and installation uses transplantation or CRISPR-based methods.
objectives: plan hierarchical assembly of a genome-scale construct
reason about error rate and verification at scale

steps.description: Break a genome design into buildable tiers, synthesise and assemble bottom-up with error checking at each level, then install and verify.
steps.intro: You cannot synthesise a chromosome in one piece - genome engineering is a hierarchy of assemblies, each verified before it becomes a part in the next.
tools: DNA synthesis + hierarchical assembly (Gibson/Golden Gate/yeast assembly)

instructions.title: Design & segment
instructions.description: Design the target sequence (e.g. recode codons, remove/refactor elements) and split it into synthesisable segments with defined junctions.

instructions.title: Assemble hierarchically
instructions.description: Build oligos to genes to cassettes to megabase segments, sequence-verifying at each tier so errors do not propagate.

instructions.title: Install
instructions.description: Introduce the synthetic DNA into a host by transplantation or iterative CRISPR-based replacement.

instructions.title: Verify function
instructions.description: Confirm the genome with long-read sequencing and test viability/phenotype of the engineered strain.

submission.description: Outline a genome-scale project (minimal genome, recoding, or a large refactor): the hierarchical assembly plan, the installation method, and how you would verify it.

resources.title: Sc2.0 - the synthetic yeast genome project
